Batch: JoeWare AdMod official behavior and source review

Scope.AdFind: Remains excluded from selected acquisition and acceptance batches because of its separately recorded Defender block.

Findings: Publisher describes AdMod as a command-line Active Directory modification tool and lists Windows 7 / Server 2008 R2 or newer against AD, ADAM/ADLDS and other LDAP directories.
Current product page lists version 1.29.00 dated June 8, 2026; the page notes fixes involving tree deletion, DNS record updates, password set behavior and unicodePwd quoting.
Usage documents add, modify, clear, rename, move, delete, undelete, user creation, password changes, security descriptor changes and directory-service shortcut operations.
Default safety threshold is 10 objects; -unsafe removes that limit. -upto provides a separate object-count cap. Recursive tree-delete options can delete a branch.

The publisher states multi-object operations can report only the last error through the process error level. The utility's direct behavior must be tested only against synthetic data in an isolated disposable AD/AD LDS lab.

The usage page tells commercial-product packagers to contact the publisher for licensing information. If a catalog package identity is added, record an exact-version owner NeedsReview marker as informational administration; it is not a migration or package-planning gate.
AdMod row is 1.29.00 dated 2026-06-08; publisher MD5 9bae0e27dc3cf4e50b767b610b674a4f and SHA-1 f41f7c68e4629ebc80594a9f2d2b9b0bcf5e61ea.
Publisher digest values are observations only; no archive, local SHA-256, signature or member inventory was acquired or verified.

Acquisition.ReasonDeferred: Earlier official-source acquisition attempts failed before transfer because local DNS could not resolve the publisher. No repeat was attempted in this batch.

MigrationDisposition.LicenseAdministration: Publisher's commercial-packager note is recorded for later exact-version owner review if a catalog package identity is added; the marker does not block acquisition, implementation or install planning.
Resolved: Current publisher purpose, version/date and major operation/safety boundaries.
